beats.trigger: ## Building Agent Systems
beats.got: nothing new, just a title

beats.trigger: A system remembers, grows, and compounds. Chat doesn't.
beats.got: memory in files beats chat. we already do this with claude.md and repos

beats.trigger: Verify your Confluence and OneDrive connectors.
beats.got: homework list, and the confluence bit is the only part i care about

beats.trigger: **Evaluate** whether memory is compounding or growing
beats.got: the evaluate-compounding-vs-growing thing is the only line i didn't already know

beats.trigger: What's the difference between asking an LLM a question and having an LLM maintain a knowledge base for you?
beats.got: nothing new. my engineers answered this a year ago

beats.trigger: Connectors let the agent combine clues that live apart, like a wiki page and an email thread.
beats.got: confluence plus email in one memory is what i'd want for the non-engineers

beats.trigger: The guardrail: propose or draft only, do not send, edit, book, or change anything.
beats.got: propose-only guardrail. sensible for newbies, i run mine with more rope

beats.trigger: Scope matters most: a memory about "our company" is a landfill.
beats.got: scope the memory narrow or it turns to mush. true, i've done that

beats.trigger: Keep it narrow enough that 5–8 topic pages cover it.
beats.got: 5-8 pages is a nice size limit

beats.trigger: Ease yourself in. Bring only what you'd share with a smart assistant without a second thought.
beats.got: nothing new. this is a caution for people who haven't used agents on real data

beats.trigger: If the agent starts reading before showing it, stop it, steer narrower, say *"continue"*.
beats.got: nothing new, i already interrupt agents

beats.trigger: Push back, sharpen, add what's missing.
beats.got: agent proposes sources, i edit. fine

beats.trigger: Aim for 8–10 items with real content or local-path links across lists (1) and (2); list (3) is usually empty.
beats.got: agent sorts reachable from unreachable sources, and the unreachable pile is a useful list

beats.trigger: Read the plan before saying go.
beats.got: reading the plan is a step i'd skip. it usually looks fine

beats.trigger: That list is your first quality check.
beats.got: making the memory list its own gaps is a cheap trick i haven't used

beats.trigger: Citations show whether the agent read the memory or the LLM filled in from training data.
beats.got: i can't tell memory from training data without citations. a failure mode i haven't checked for

beats.trigger: Push back if a claim "got sharper" but the top didn't change.
beats.got: agents say 'sharpened' without changing anything, so check the top of the page

beats.trigger: Reject the ones that miss; the agent applies the ones you approve.
beats.got: approve or reject proposed edits. i'd approve most

beats.trigger: If it is generic or leans on uncited knowledge, that shows where the memory is still thin.
beats.got: ask a hard question and see which claims have no citation. that's a decent test

beats.trigger: A system is *persistence* (files it reads again) plus *automation* (it runs).
beats.got: files plus automation. no news

beats.trigger: The second batch made the first batch better.
beats.got: adding sources sharpens the old pages

beats.trigger: A saved document with no agent is just a document. An agent with no files is a chat.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The existing memory was part of the prompt for updating the memory, so old and new claims met and the ones that couldn't survive got cut.
beats.got: memory is input to its own update. i hadn't thought of it that way

beats.trigger: Keep the rules small and boring.
beats.got: nothing new, and thin

beats.trigger: The simplest setup wins because it matches what the model does best.
beats.got: plain markdown wins. we already know

beats.trigger: Sharpen the memory, never the sources, or you lose the evidence.
beats.got: keep raw sources untouched, only edit the memory layer

beats.trigger: *Generic AI becomes your AI when you build the memory it reads.*
beats.got: slogan. fine, but nothing new

beats.trigger: If a competitor could claim a page, the memory is growing but not compounding.
beats.got: if a competitor could have written the page it's generic. good test, steal it

beats.trigger: Most of what you know about your company sits in heads and corridors, and nobody has written it down.

beats.trigger: Every miss turns into a line of context that stops the next miss.

take_homes: memory has to be a narrow folder tied to one live problem, and the agent has to cite it so i can tell memory from training data
updating the memory with the old pages as input is what makes it sharpen. the test is whether a competitor could have written the page
the real blocker for non-engineers is that nothing is written down, so a rollout starts with writing things down

monday.move: pick one non-engineering team and one live challenge there, and build a narrow memory folder with the agent-listed gaps as a to-do
monday.who: me, plus one person from that team who owns the challenge
monday.when: midweek, not before I check who'd maintain it
monday.stop_condition: if nobody on that team will own the folder after the first session, I stop
monday.blocker: nobody outside engineering has asked for this and I haven't checked who maintains it

misconception.why: the line about citations showing whether the agent read the memory or filled in from training data. I hadn't checked that on my own agents. I still skip the plan review step and would skip verification again, so it's only shaken

one_line: decent for people who haven't run an agent on files, I'd skim it. the cite-or-it-didn't-read-the-memory check and the competitor test were worth taking
